label: def:rigid-monoidal-category
title: Rigid monoidal category
html:
Definition. Rigid monoidal category

A monoidal category (\mathbf{C}, \otimes, \mathbf{1}) is a category equipped with a bifunctor \otimes \colon \mathbf{C} \times \mathbf{C} \to \mathbf{C}, a unit object \mathbf{1}, and natural isomorphisms expressing associativity and unitality:

\begin{equation}\label{eq:monoidal-axioms}
\begin{gathered}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=3em]
  (X \otimes Y) \otimes Z
    \ar[r, "\alpha_{X,Y,Z}", "\sim"']
  & X \otimes (Y \otimes Z)
\end{tikzcd}
\\[-0.5em]
\text{\small (associativity)}
\end{gathered}
\qquad
\begin{gathered}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5em]
  \mathbf{1} \otimes X
    \ar[r, "\ell_X", "\sim"']
  & X
  & X \otimes \mathbf{1}
    \ar[l, "\rho_X"', "\sim"]
\end{tikzcd}
\\[-0.5em]
\text{\small (unitality)}
\end{gathered}
\end{equation}

The category is rigid if every object V has a dual V^{\vee} together with morphisms \mathrm{ev}_V \colon V \otimes V^{\vee} \to \mathbf{1} and \mathrm{coev}_V \colon \mathbf{1} \to V^{\vee} \otimes V satisfying the snake identities.

We say \mathbf{C} is R-linear for a commutative ring R without quasi-zeros if every hom-set is an R-module and composition is R-bilinear.

The category is braided monoidal if it has a natural isomorphism c_{X,Y} \colon X \otimes Y \xrightarrow{\sim} Y \otimes X compatible with the associator and satisfying the hexagon axioms. The braiding is symmetric when c_{Y,X} \circ c_{X,Y} = \mathrm{id}. Given a braiding, the exterior power \Lambda^k V is the image of the antisymmetriser \mathrm{Alt}_k = \sum_{\pi \in S_k} \mathrm{sgn}(\pi)\pi acting on V^{\otimes k}, where permutations act via c.
